title: Clean up duplicate sections in an AI-built wiki
summary: The Synthadoc team had an AI fix flagged wiki pages for approval; they report it rewrote pages, kept weak duplicates and leaked notes until they added checks.
agent_role: A simple scanner flags problems; the AI proposes fixes; a person reviews a before-and-after view and approves, with a saved copy for undo.
outcome: The authors report five failure types and the safeguards they added to catch them; no success rate is given.
what_they_did: The makers of Synthadoc, an open-source wiki that builds pages from documents, built a cleanup step. A plain script flags repeated or thin sections. An AI proposes fixes, the user sees before and after, and approves before anything is saved.
how_it_went: They say the AI first rewrote whole pages, kept a short duplicate over one with citations, leaked file-reading commands, left planning notes, and dropped a year it thought was wrong. They added output cleaning and draft detection.
worth_knowing: Telling the AI 'keep the first copy' was precise but wrong; the rule needed to be 'keep the best'. Better instructions alone did not stop failures, so they also kept the approval step and undo.
prompt: Review the Markdown pages in [wiki folder]. List every page with repeated headings, empty sections or very short sections. For each problem, propose the smallest fix: merge duplicates by keeping the most detailed version with its citations, and never rename headings, change dates or add facts that are not on the page. Show each change as a before-and-after view and wait for my approval. Save a copy of the original before writing anything.

curation.rationale: A detailed, honest account of an open-source workflow where an AI fixes wiki pages with human approval, listing five concrete failures and fixes; strong on lessons but no numeric results.
